title: The edge of special relativity: tides, free fall and the road to curvature
summary: Free fall as the free-float frame; the local character of inertial frames and tidal accelerations; the parable of the two travellers; gravitation as curvature announced as a preview of PHY-240; gravitational time dilation and light bending as equivalence-principle consequences; what special relativity has established and under what hypotheses.

objectives.description: Objectives will be finalised when the unit is prepared; the source material is Spacetime Physics Chapter 9 and Section 2.3, and MIT 8.20 Week 4 (Lectures 12.1–12.6).

preparation.description: Read Spacetime Physics Chapter 9 Gravity: Curved Spacetime in Action (pp. 275–298), treating 9.7–9.9 as orientation only.
Re-read Chapter 2, Section 2.3 Local Character of Free-Float Frame (pp. 30–34).
Optional: MIT 8.20 Week 4 videos, Lectures 12.1–12.6 (equivalence principle, gravitational time dilation, light bending, redshift tests, general relativity, experimental evidence).

activities.title: Reading: the edge of special relativity
activities.instructions: Read the listed material for this unit, keeping a written list of every statement that goes beyond flat spacetime; the prepared lesson will label each as a preview of PHY-240. The prepared lesson, tutorial and exercises are not yet written; this outline shows exactly what the unit will cover.
